title: Étale inverse image: abelian lift and hom-set comparison
statement: Let U and V be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and f : U → V any morphism. On their small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let L = Scheme.etaleSetPullback f be the set inverse image [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and assume L preserves finite limits. Let La and Ra be the abelian inverse and direct images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] on abelian étale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Let FaU and FaV forget abelian sheaves to set sheaves, and a be the set adjunction. There is a natural isomorphism ea : La ⋙ FaU ≅ FaV ⋙ L such that for all G, F and h : La G → F, FaV(a_ab.homEquiv G F h) = a.homEquiv (FaV G) (FaU F) (ea_G⁻¹ ≫ FaU(h)). For every G, its sectionwise addition, zero and negation are sheaf morphisms addV, zeroV, negV; those of La G are addU, zeroU, negU. They satisfy L(addV) = prodComparison L ≫ prod.map ea_G⁻¹ ea_G⁻¹ ≫ addU ≫ ea_G, L(zeroV) = terminal.from _ ≫ zeroU ≫ ea_G, and L(negV) = ea_G⁻¹ ≫ negU ≫ ea_G. The binary operation formulas use the two chosen product projections, and the constant formulas hold on every section of the chosen terminal sheaf. No unit compatibility or ring assertion is assumed in this lemma.

proof.text: The base-change functor is continuous. The recorded set inverse image is left adjoint to its sectionwise set direct image by Mathlib.sheafAdjunctionContinuous. The assumed finite-limit preservation implies finite-product preservation.

Use the abelian clause of the sheaf/internal-object identification on the source and target sites; its section formulas identify the structure maps with the actual sectionwise operations. Apply the corresponding clause of the product-preserving lifted adjunction to the set adjunction.

Transport the lifted adjunction through the inverse sheaf/internal-object functors. Its right lift evaluates at base-changed objects and hence has exactly the sectionwise operations and restriction maps of the recorded direct image. The resulting right forgetful comparison is the identity; restrict the hom-set equations of the generic lift accordingly.

Compare the transported left adjoint with Etale.upperStar, another left adjoint of the same abelian direct image, using the unique isomorphism compatible with the adjunctions. Composing its underlying comparison with that of the internal-object lift gives ea. The compatibility of adjunction bijections gives precisely the displayed hom-set equation.

Take the sectionwise operations supplied by the sheaf/internal-object identification. Transport the left-adjoint comparison across them. Naturality of the product comparison gives the binary-operation equations after composing with its inverse and cancelling the isomorphism. For constants use uniqueness of the map to the terminal sheaf, and for negation use the inverse comparison component. The section formulas are the source and target identification formulas.
